messages:
lisa: Heads-up — noticed a pattern where EU customers on standard tier are being routed to us-east during spike windows. Adds ~220ms and some 5xxs. Can someone sanity-check routing policy?

olga: I saw that too in traces. Looks like region selection went to cost-priority path when EU capacity dropped below threshold.

kevin: Yep. Current policy is "tier -> cost-first for standard, latency-first for premium" with a simple fallback to any compatible region. Problem is we treat "compatible" as any model name match and ignore quantization/variant constraints.

maria: That explains the 5xxs — the us-east pool only has the int8-quant variant and we were asking for fp16 in-region preference, so runtime tried to route and failed then fell back incorrectly.

sam: Proposed fix: introduce weighted probing + strict variant preference. Algorithm: probe N regions ordered by weighted score (latency SLO, capacity slack, tier penalty) and pick first region that reports both healthy and has a compatible variant; if none match variant, decide whether to accept variant downgrade based on customer tier and a per-candidate score.

olga: Sketch of policy YAML I put together:
```yaml
routing_policy:
  probe_count: 3 # how many regions to actively probe
  score_weights:
    latency_ms: 0.5
    capacity_slack: 0.3
    cost_delta_pct: 0.2
  tiers:
    premium:
      variant_preference: [fp16, int8, int4] # strict order
      allow_variant_downgrade: false
    standard:
      variant_preference: [fp16, int8, int4]
      allow_variant_downgrade: true
      downgrade_cost_threshold_pct: 30
  fallback_chain: [same_region_compatible, nearest_region_variant, nearest_region_any_variant]
```

lisa: That looks reasonable. A few questions: how do we compute capacity_slack? is it instantaneous, averaged? Also need to ensure probes don't increase p95 latency.

kevin: Capacity slack = (available_tokens / configured_pool_capacity) smoothed over 1 min by default. We can expose smoothing window in config. For probes: use passive probing when possible (recent health checks + last RTT) and active only when passive is stale. Active probe timeout must be < region selection budget (say 30ms).

maria: Console UX: we should show resolved routing decision per-request in the console traces: selected_region, selected_variant, decision_score_breakdown. That will make rollouts and A/B easier for SRE and customers.

olga: Agreed. Add telemetry keys: 
- routing.selected_region
- routing.selected_variant
- routing.decision_scores: list
- routing.probe_latency_ms
- routing.fallback_reason

sam: Also important: quota interactions. If premium has reserved capacity in eu-west, we must prefer that even if slightly higher latency. So score should add hard bonuses for reserved_capacity allocations.

kevin: Implementation plan:
1) Add routing score computation + variant matching in routing service (runtime)
2) Add probe cache + passive fallback in routing agent
3) Add telemetry keys and wire to console traces
4) Add rollout flag behind feature gate for 2% of traffic per org (configurable)

lisa: Can we make downgrade decisions explicit in the API response? e.g., response header or metadata: "variant_used" and "variant_reason" so customers can detect quality regressions?

maria: Yes — add to trace and to the HTTP response metadata under "x-redwood-routing". Also add a rollback hook: if quality regressions detected (evals), we can auto-disable downgrade for that org.

deploy-bot: deploy started for routing-service/routing-score-v2 @ 1773003500 by kevin — canary 2% -> 10%

kevin: Deploy in progress. If anyone has objections to the score weights above, speak now.

olga: Minor tweak: increase latency weight for premium to 0.7, drop cost to 0.1.

sam: Fine with me. Also recommend telemetry alert: anomalous increase in "routing.fallback_reason:nearest_region_any_variant" for a customer => auto-investigate.

lisa: Action items:
- kevin: implement scoring + probe cache (ETA 3d)
- olga: add telemetry keys + console trace fields (ETA 2d)
- maria: API metadata header + rollout UX (ETA 4d)
- sam: write doc for policy and onboard SRE runbook (ETA 1w)

kevin: Acknowledged. Will follow up with PRs.

maria: One more note — we should ensure the quota/usage dashboard shows variant-level token accounting. Otherwise cost reconciliation will be messy when downgrades happen.

lisa: Great catch. Add that to the runbook.

sam: OK closing thread — follow-ups in PRs. :thumbsup:
